records._note: TSK-009. Antitrust fine (EU 2009 / Intel): the common effect announces the fine, the choices are pay, pay into a reserve, appeal. caseId = Args[4]. All numbers of the case are here.
TSK-009. Consent decree (FTC 1998 / Intel): settle (remedy, no fine) or fight (legal costs, then 50 % closed / 50 % remedy and a fine of 1 % of revenue).
TSK-009. The new, smaller fine after an annulment; fired by CaseService itself (Args[4] = caseId). The numbers are those of the case.

TSK-010. A victim's suit (AMD v Intel 2009). Fired for the plaintiff (Args[3] = the defendant, Args[4] = the case). The suit needs 10 % of the market over 36 months. Numbers: settlementDefaults of params.json.
TSK-011. The export rule comes into force (stage 0 of hist.2022.exportcontrol). Global: the effect works on the market. ruleId = Args[4].
TSK-011. The second stage (2023-10-17): a new percentile and a larger share, the same rule.

TSK-011. The answer of a company with a CPU above the threshold (onlyIf of the calendar). A licence pays licenseCostPct of the revenue and works with licenseSuccess; lobbying halves the blocked share on success.
TSK-011. The same answers at the second stage.

TSK-012. The aggressor of a price war. The war of the entry is in the extra arguments of the fire: [warId, "segments joined by |;cut;followCut;durationDays"] (Args[4], Args[5]); what they leave out comes from priceWarDefaults of params.json and the code.
TSK-012. The player who is not the aggressor: follow, hold, or answer with marketing (marketingCostPct of the revenue, popularity.gain x1.10 for 180 days).

TSK-013. The plaintiff of a patent dispute (the player; an AI plaintiff goes straight to the defendant's event). Args[3] = the defendant, Args[4] = disputeId, Args[5] = the kind of dispute (licenseWithdrawal or infringement).
TSK-013. The defendant of a licence withdrawal (AMD v Intel 1987): the common effect opens the dispute (Args[3] = the plaintiff); the numbers are disputeDefaults of params.json.
TSK-013. The defendant accused of copying a design (Intel v Cyrix 1992).
